boundary_decision.rationale: Two axes must not be conflated. On the record plane a registry value such as standalone-mm describes how the model record is stored, versioned and governed in the registry; it is never a subject-model entry kind, and here frozen_context was empty so no frozen registry value could be read at all - that absence is carried as a publication hold rather than silently resolved. On the subject axis the most defensible schema kind is aggregate: the booking has one root identity (authoritative source plus booking identifier plus current lineage head), a transactional confirmation invariant that binds current capacity to required participant responses, and it composes proposals, responses, booking-scoped party roles, status events and booking-specific evidence that have no independent life outside the root, while party, resource, service, place, schedule, slot, order, payment, message, encounter and audit masters remain external references. event is rejected despite the display name because the record is a mutable, revisioned, long-lived commitment whose typed transitions are constituents rather than the root; entity understates the owned composition and append-only lineage; relationship understates independent identity, terms, communications and lifecycle; pattern, mixin, registry and classifier do not describe an instance-bearing subject at all.

decisions.rationale: One root identity plus lineage head, an atomic confirmation invariant over capacity and required responses, and owned proposals, responses, roles and status events satisfy aggregate semantics better than entity, event or relationship.

decisions.disposition: rejected as an aggregate-root label; rename deferred
decisions.rationale: The word Event collides with the schema kind event and with the model's own out-of-scope actual occurrence, inviting exactly the confusion the Encounter boundary note tries to prevent. A draft may publish under the current name only with the rename hold visible.

decisions.concept: Record-plane registry value used as subject entry kind
decisions.rationale: A record-plane classifier such as standalone-mm answers how the record is governed, not what the subject is; with frozen_context empty there is additionally no verified registry value to copy, so the entry kind is set from subject evidence alone.

decisions.disposition: rejected as written; occurrence discriminator required
decisions.rationale: SRC-005 and SRC-007 identify a single occurrence by series identifier plus recurrence identifier. If booking-id resolves to the series, occurrence-scoped artifacts for an overridden or excluded instance are ambiguous, which breaks the model's own artifact identity guarantee.

decisions.concept: Question kind labels across all 72 questions
decisions.disposition: rejected as semantic metadata; re-typing deferred
decisions.rationale: The same three templated texts carry rotating kinds - one identical 'What identity, type, role, scope, version and values define X?' shape appears as identity, definition, relationship, requirement, ownership, classification, composition and state. The kind axis is positional, not semantic, and must not be presented as a taxonomy.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist rows relationships, retention and deletion, interoperability
decisions.rationale: No approved relation rows exist, no redaction rule covers personal data inside append-only lineage, and the crosswalk names five formats without enumerating field or state mappings while TMF646 v5 remains unreviewed. Sixteen of sixteen covered is an overclaim at draft stage.

decisions.concept: Capacity hold ownership between booking and slot or schedule
decisions.disposition: accepted with an explicit boundary qualifier
decisions.rationale: SRC-002 and SRC-003 keep capacity, availability and hold expiry with the slot and schedule owners. The booking may record a source-qualified hold reference, deadline and its own expectation, but must not be read as decrementing or enforcing capacity; the function name place-or-release-temporary-hold needs the record-only qualifier its description already states.

decisions.concept: Arrived, checked-in, no-show and fulfilled states inside booking lifecycle
decisions.disposition: accepted as source-grounded assertions; rejected as proof
decisions.rationale: SRC-001 carries these in FHIR R5 Appointment status, so their presence is sourced rather than invented, but the declared conflict and adversarial check that status never proves attendance or service performance must survive into every published projection.

decisions.disposition: rejected as one capability; split deferred
decisions.rationale: It fuses agent-allowlisted validation with authority-gated correction and destructive disposition, contradicting the policy that agents may validate and project freely while disposition requires delegated authority. Under the single-provider waiver add_functions must stay empty, so this is carried as a hold rather than repaired here.

decisions.concept: Missing waitlist enrollment, promotion and expiry function
decisions.rationale: Waitlist appears in the purpose, in_scope list and the proposed-held-pending-confirmed-waitlisted status finding, yet no function covers enrollment, position, promotion or lapse. The gap is recorded because no second provider exists to supply the function.

decisions.concept: RFC 3339 timestamp rule with no RFC 3339 source row
decisions.disposition: rejected as unsourced; pin before promotion
decisions.rationale: artifact_rules impose a normative RFC 3339 format requirement while the only adjacent source is SRC-008 RFC 9557, which extends rather than defines that format. A normative rule must cite the standard it enforces.

decisions.concept: Uniform artifact media_or_form across all 24 artifacts
decisions.disposition: accepted for the logical layer; media differentiation deferred
decisions.rationale: A single logical booking assertion form is coherent at draft, but the crosswalk and communications artifacts claim loss-aware projection and an integrity rule that stores media type, which cannot be tested without concrete serializations such as text/calendar, JSCalendar JSON and FHIR JSON.

decisions.concept: Bundle cohesion of terms, commerce, communications, evidence and provenance
decisions.rationale: The perfectly uniform six-by-two-by-two grid forced commerce terms and provenance or quality into one bundle. The content is sound but the decomposition is template-driven rather than domain-driven and should be revisited before canonical promotion.

decisions.concept: Cross-participant disclosure of responses and contact endpoints
decisions.rationale: The access default denies contact endpoints and history, but never adjudicates whether one participant may see another participant's response state or delegation, which SRC-005 and SRC-006 make a live interoperability and privacy decision rather than an implementation detail.

decisions.concept: Erasure of personal data inside append-only confirmed history
decisions.rationale: Tombstones, legal hold and disposition authority exist, but no rule governs redaction or pseudonymization of participant identifiers, contacts and free-text purpose embedded in retained proposals, responses and message references, leaving append-only lineage and erasure obligations unreconciled.

decisions.concept: Service layers under the single-provider waiver
decisions.rationale: merge_service_layers stays true only for schema compatibility; with no admitted second provider the deterministic synthesizer has nothing to merge, so the dimension, canon, artifact, policy, CRUD, role, access and bootstrap blocks publish verbatim as single-source content and must be labelled as such.

deferred_research: Review the current TM Forum appointment management specification, including any v5 profile, against the SRC-011 v4.0.1 material and reconcile state, hold and capacity semantics.

Enumerate the field-level and state-level crosswalk between FHIR R5 Appointment and AppointmentResponse, RFC 5545 and 5546, RFC 8984 JSCalendar, Schema.org Reservation and TMF646, with a round-trip test corpus and a declared loss class per direction.

Define a redaction and pseudonymization rule for personal data embedded in append-only proposals, responses, communications references and status events, reconciled with legal hold, tombstone minima and jurisdictional erasure rights.

Adjudicate cross-participant disclosure: whether a participant may see other participants' response state, delegation chain, contact endpoints or virtual location, grounded in ITIP and JSCalendar participant visibility semantics.
Specify waitlist enrollment, position, promotion, lapse and notification operations, and split the hold lifecycle authority explicitly between the booking aggregate and the slot or schedule steward.

Develop sector booking profiles for transport, lodging, dining, healthcare procedures, court hearings and workforce dispatch, and derive the precedence rules for a confirmed booking coexisting with stale availability, a participant decline, a failed payment or a provider-side cancellation.
Add an explicit source row for the base timestamp standard enforced by artifact_rules and confirm that named time-zone intent survives recurrence expansion after time-zone rule changes.
publication_holds: Live source and version verification is outstanding for all twelve sources; verify every URL resolves and every pin is exact before promotion, with priority on SRC-009 and SRC-010 Schema.org V30.0 dated 19 March 2026, SRC-011 TMF646 whose URL slug reads r19-0-0 against a declared v4.0.1 of November 2019, and the four FHIR R5 5.0.0 resource anchors.

Independent second-provider review is absent by explicit repository-owner authorization dated 2026-09-06: Claude was waived after repeated timeouts and Grok was waived as unavailable. This audit is a local no-tools adversarial pass over the codex result and does not constitute external review; the waiver and this limitation must appear in every published artifact.

The record stays reviewable-draft, never canonical, while the frozen registry record is unavailable - frozen_context was supplied empty, so the record-plane classification, registry lineage and prior entry-kind history for vr.wm-act-026 could not be checked against the published subject kind.

No approved relation rows were supplied; all neighbor links to Encounter and to party, resource, service, location, schedule, slot, order, payment, message, evidence and audit models publish as proposals under the relationship contract and must not be rendered as accepted edges.

Artifact identity is not yet normative: the serial naming rule needs an occurrence discriminator for recurring series, and the question-kind axis must be re-typed semantically or demoted to a non-normative rotation marker, before either is cited as a governance guarantee.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
